_comment: ngsolve contact#3 (a flipped contact normal makes the penalty push the bodies together). Run 2026-08-06 on NGSolve 6.2.2604: elastic block E=1000 nu=0.3 on maxh 0.2, fixed on top, body force 150 onto a floor 0.01 below, penalty on the bottom edge, the flipped case being the same energy with the opposite sign -- which is the residual a wrong-signed normal produces. The diagnostic the claim recommends is verified first: specialcf.normal(2) integrated over the bottom edge is (0,-1) and over the top edge (0,+1), so the check discriminates. Against a no-contact reference run (penetration 5.59e-2), the correct sign separates (3.02e-2) and the flipped sign pushes in (4.74e-1), and the flipped penetration grows 7.75x per decade of gamma -- the claim's 'without bound'. The part worth keeping: every flipped run returns ngsolve.solvers.Newton status 0. Solver status is not a guard against a wrong-signed normal. Mutation: forcing the flipped branch to use the correct sign makes the two runs identical and the fixture fails on flipped_sign_pushes_in.
